meta.title: The Shelter Dog
meta.blurb: Farofa is nine years old, and she has lived at the animal shelter for three years. Nobody has ever chosen her. Can Bia find her a home? It depends on you.

p1.title: Three Years Waiting
text: Bia had always wanted a dog, but her apartment was too small. So, for a community project at school, she chose to do [[volunteer work|trabalho voluntário]] at Patas Amigas, a small animal [[shelter|abrigo]].

On her first Saturday, Dona Célia, who runs the shelter, showed her around. First, they visited the [[puppies|filhotes]]. “Puppies never stay here for long,” she said. “Families [[adopt|adotam]] them in a few days.”
Then they stopped at the last [[kennel|baia do canil]]. An old brown dog with a gray face was lying on a blanket. She slowly moved her tail.

“This is Farofa,” said Dona Célia. “She's nine years old, and she's [[blind|cega]] in one eye. She has lived here for three years. Hundreds of families have visited us since then, but nobody has ever chosen her.”
Bia sat down next to the kennel, and Farofa put her nose against her hand. “The [[adoption fair|feira de adoção]] is next month,” said Dona Célia. “But old dogs don't usually have much luck there.”

p2a.title: The Perfect Photo
text: Bia's friend Rafa was the best photographer in their class, so she asked for his help. On Sunday, they took Farofa to the shelter's garden. However, she was too slow for action photos, and she kept closing her eyes in the sun.

After an hour, they had taken more than two hundred photos. Then Rafa found an old picture on the shelter's computer. It showed Farofa six years earlier: she was running on the beach, young and full of energy.
“Look at this one!” he said. “If we post this photo and say she's five, she'll have a family in a day. Nobody has ever adopted her with the real photos, right?”
Bia looked at the old photo, and then at the real Farofa, who was sleeping under a tree. The new photos were honest, but they weren't very exciting.

p2b.title: Slow Walks
text: Bia started visiting the shelter every Saturday and two afternoons a week after school. At first, Farofa walked very slowly and stopped at every tree. However, after a few weeks, she was waiting at the gate every time Bia arrived.
Bia also taught her to sit and to give her [[paw|pata]]. “Nobody has ever taught her anything,” said Dona Célia, surprised. “You've done more for her in a month than we've done in three years.”
One afternoon, while they were walking around the square, Bia noticed an old man on a bench. He was feeding the [[pigeons|pombos]], and he was watching Farofa with a smile.
“She looks like a dog I had when I was a boy,” he said. “I've lived alone for five years, you know.” His name was Seu Antônio.
Later, Bia thought about him. The adoption fair was in two weeks.

p3x.title: A Possible Home

text.text: Bia posted the new photos with an honest text: “Farofa is nine. She can't see with one eye, and she walks slowly. But she has the kindest heart in the shelter.” The post didn't get many likes. But two days later, a message arrived:

text.msg: Hello! My name is Antônio. I'm 72, and I've lived alone for five years. My granddaughter has just shown me your post. Can I meet Farofa?

text.text: The next Saturday, Bia took Farofa to the square. Seu Antônio was sitting on the same bench. Farofa walked straight to him and put her head on his knee, as if they were old friends.

text: “I've never had a dog as an adult,” Seu Antônio told Bia when they met. “Do you think I could take care of her?”
However, his son, Márcio, was worried. “Dad, you're 72,” he said. “What if she gets sick? What if you fall during a walk?”
Seu Antônio [[sighed|suspirou]]. “Maybe he's right. I haven't taken care of anyone for a long time.” Then Bia had two ideas.

p3y.title: Five Hundred Likes
text: In two days, the post had more than five hundred likes and forty shares. Bia had never seen so many hearts on her phone. “I told you!” said Rafa.

On Saturday, the Moura family arrived at the shelter: a mother, a father and two [[energetic|cheios de energia]] boys with a football. “Where's the dog from the photo?” asked the youngest boy. “We want to play football with her!”

Dona Célia brought Farofa out. She walked slowly towards the boys and [[bumped into|esbarrou em]] a chair. The father [[frowned|franziu a testa]]. “This dog isn't five,” he said. “She's old, and she can't see well!”
Later, Dona Célia called Bia into her office. “Have you ever thought about what happens when a family feels [[cheated|enganada]]?” she asked. “They bring the dog back. I've seen it many times.”

p3z.title: Busy Weeks
text: Bia decided to wait for the fair. Meanwhile, the end of the term arrived, and with it came tests, projects and a [[presentation|apresentação]] in her programming class. One Saturday, she stayed home to study. Then she missed another one, and another.
After three weeks, she finally returned to the shelter. Farofa didn't come to the gate. She was lying in the corner of her kennel, and she only moved her tail a little.
“She hasn't eaten well since you stopped coming,” said Dona Célia. “I think she has missed you.”
Bia felt terrible. Suddenly, she remembered something: the adoption fair was on the next Saturday, and she still had two tests that week.

p4a.title: Two Old Friends
text: For the next two weeks, Bia met Seu Antônio and Farofa at the square every Tuesday and Thursday. First, she showed him how to use the [[leash|guia (coleira)]]. Then she taught him Farofa's favorite words: “sit”, “paw” and “cookie”.
Seu Antônio learned fast. He bought a soft bed, a water bowl and a [[ramp|rampa]] for his front door, because Farofa couldn't climb stairs very well.
One afternoon, while they were walking, Márcio's car stopped next to them. He watched his father laughing with the old dog, and he smiled. “Dad, I haven't seen you this happy for years,” he said.
Later, Seu Antônio asked Bia: “Should I adopt her now? Or should we take her to the fair first, so people can see that old dogs are great?”

p4b.title: The Adoption Fair

text.text: Bia deleted the old post and wrote a new one: “I lied about Farofa's age, and I'm sorry. She's nine, and she's the sweetest dog I've ever met.” Some people [[criticized|criticaram]] her, but many shared the new post.
Seu Antônio and Márcio promised to come to the fair. “I want to see the dog with my own eyes,” Márcio said.
Bia studied every night that week. Then, on Friday afternoon, she gave Farofa a bath and put a red [[bandana|lenço]] around her neck. Rafa made a sign: “9 years old. 1 good eye. 100% love.”

text: The fair was in the town square. It was full of noise, music and puppies. Families walked past Farofa's corner, looked at her for a second and went to the puppies.
Then, while Bia was talking to a family, a [[loudspeaker|caixa de som]] suddenly started playing music very loudly. Farofa [[trembled|tremeu]] and hid behind Bia's legs.
On the stage, Dona Célia was presenting the dogs with a microphone. Bia looked at the stage, and then at the shaking dog.

p4c.title: The Trial Week
text: “Just try for one week,” Bia told the Mouras. “She's very sweet. You'll love her.” Finally, the father agreed, but he didn't look happy.

On the first day, the boys threw the ball for Farofa. She looked at it and lay down. On the second day, she bumped into a table and broke a vase. On the third day, she hid under a bed and didn't come out.

On the fourth day, Bia's phone rang. It was Mr. Moura. “She's a good dog,” he said, “but she isn't the dog from the photo. My kids are [[disappointed|decepcionados]], and I feel cheated. What should we do?”
Bia looked at the old photo on her phone. She had wanted to help Farofa. Had she only made things worse?

p4d.title: Test Week
text: Bia studied all week. On Saturday, while the fair was happening in the square, she was sitting at her desk with her books. She got good grades on both tests. Even so, she felt strange.
On Sunday night, Rafa sent her a message:

text.msg: The fair was great! 23 dogs have found homes. Farofa hasn't. Dona Célia said she spent the day lying in a corner. Are you coming back to the shelter?

text: Bia read the message three times. Then she put the phone down. She thought about Farofa's gray face at the gate. Then she thought about her project: she had already done all the volunteer hours. She didn't really need to go back.

e1.title: A Home at Last
text: Seu Antônio adopted Farofa on a Wednesday afternoon. Dona Célia cried a little when she said goodbye. “I've seen hundreds of adoptions,” she said, “but this one is special.”

Bia kept her promise. After that, every Saturday, she walked to Seu Antônio's house after her volunteer work. He was always waiting at the door with coffee, and Farofa was always waiting with her tail.
A few months later, Márcio sent Bia a photo: his father and Farofa on the beach, both with gray hair, both very happy. Under the photo, he wrote: “Thank you. You've given my father a friend.”
e1.eventPt: o Seu Antônio adotou a Farofa

options: She gave his father a friend

e2.title: The Star of the Fair
text: At the fair, Bia took the microphone. “Everybody loves puppies,” she began. “But this is Farofa. She has lived in our shelter for three years. She's slow, and she can't see with one eye. But she has never bitten anyone, and she has waited longer than any dog here.”
The square went quiet. Then people started to clap.

text.text: Finally, Seu Antônio walked to the stage and took the leash. “She's coming home with me,” he said. Márcio was standing next to him, smiling.
Finally, an old woman came to the stage. “I'm seventy, and I'm slow too,” she said, laughing. “We'll be perfect together.” Her name was Dona Lúcia.

text: In the end, five old dogs found homes that day, and the shelter started a new campaign: “Adopt an old friend.”

e3.title: A Second Try
text: Bia went to the Mouras' house and took Farofa back to the shelter. The boys were sad, but their father looked [[relieved|aliviado]]. In the car, Farofa put her head on Bia's lap and fell asleep.
That night, Bia deleted the old post. Then she wrote a new one, with the real photos and the whole truth. It didn't get five hundred likes. It got thirty-two.

However, one of those thirty-two was from a [[retired|aposentada]] teacher. “I don't want a dog for football,” she wrote. “I want a dog for long, slow afternoons. Can I visit Farofa?” This time, the right person was looking for her.
e3.event: Bia took Farofa back and wrote an honest post
e3.eventPt: a Bia levou a Farofa de volta e escreveu uma publicação sincera

e4.title: The Shelter's Dog
text: Farofa didn't find a family at the fair. In fact, nobody adopted her that year. But Bia didn't give up, and something changed.

text.text: Márcio still didn't like the idea of a dog in his father's house. So instead, Seu Antônio became a volunteer too, and he visited Farofa every Sunday.

text: Dona Célia moved Farofa's bed from the kennel to her office, next to the window. From then on, Farofa [[greeted|cumprimentava]] every visitor at the door, slowly, with her tail moving like a flag.
Bia has visited her every Saturday since then. Her class has also made a website with the stories of the twelve oldest dogs in the shelter, and three of them have already found homes.
“Farofa hasn't found a family yet,” Bia told her teacher. “But she has found a home.”
e4.eventPt: a Farofa virou a cadela do abrigo

e5.title: Back in the Kennel
text: Bia told the Mouras that Farofa only needed time. They kept her for one more month.

However, things didn't get better. The boys stopped playing with her, and she spent most of the day alone in the backyard. Then, one rainy morning in November, the father brought her back to the shelter. She was thinner, and she was afraid of everybody.

Dona Célia didn't say anything. She didn't need to. Bia looked at the old photo on her phone, the one with the young dog running on the beach, and finally deleted it. It was the first true thing she had done for Farofa in a long time.

e6.title: The Empty Gate
text: Bia promised herself that she would go back after the tests. But then there was a birthday party, a trip to the beach and a new series to watch. Weeks became months.
In March, she walked past the shelter by chance. Through the gate, she saw a new volunteer, a boy from the first year. He was walking an old brown dog with a gray face. Farofa was still there.
Dona Célia saw Bia at the gate and waved. Bia only waved back and kept walking. She had wanted to change Farofa's life. In the end, she hadn't even said goodbye.
